title: Close CSV rerun recovery audit gaps
summary: Close CSV rerun audit gaps across fail-closed process-tree cleanup, exact durable recovery correlation and generations, verified scratch continuation, and full-chain reparse-safe scratch handling.
reason: The prior lifecycle hardening packet closed broad visibility and outage-recovery defects, but completion review found paths that could release a launch lease while a child remained alive, authorize recovery from partial correlation, strand a failed-before-manifest generation, discard a complete scratch copy after source loss, trust a scratch anchor without proving its ancestors, or delete attempt evidence after boundary proof became ambiguous.
behavior_before: A degraded process-tree kill could be treated as successful launch cleanup; waiting recovery accepted partial correlation; the first recovery enrollment permanently owned a recovery key after failed_before_manifest; equivalent Windows selector paths could split exactly-once identity; staging reprobed the source before accepting a complete landed copy; and scratch trust/cleanup checks did not prove every ancestor or preserve all ambiguous attempt evidence.
behavior_after: Launch cleanup proves exact child/tree exit or retains monotonic kill_degraded ownership; waiting recovery requires the full durable command/launch/batch/path chain; failed-before-manifest generations supersede only with literal exit/nonduplicate proof and an exactly absent expected manifest; Windows-equivalent selectors share one recovery namespace; full-hash-verified scratch continues after source loss; and scratch creation, promotion, and cleanup require a full drive/UNC-share reparse-free chain while preserving ambiguous evidence.
